title: Console essentiality trimmer: prioritization, acceptance checklist, and QA gating for dashboards/tracing/costs
creator: Sophie Grant
description: Purpose: Narrow the initial Redwood Console telemetry surface so we can ship a reliable, low-cost v1 that meets SLOs while leaving hooks for phased expansion. This ticket scopes explicit feature removals and behavior changes across: route-level dashboards, distributed tracing sampling UI, and the per-route cost breakdown widget. The goal is to create a deterministic acceptance checklist that QA, Eng, and Design can use to sign off on the trimmed MVP. Context: multiple stakeholders asked to reduce token/compute billing and rollout complexity for alpha customers. Constraints: 1) limit data retention to 7 days for v1 insights, 2) reduce per-request tokenization/embedding lookups by disabling optional enrichment, 3) keep trace visualization to sampled spans only (no full flamegraph). Scope decisions here should be reversible (feature flags) and instrumented with metrics so we can measure customer impact and re-enable items quickly if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: baseline card set (Routes, Errors, Avg latency, Token cost) implemented with configurable time windows; no more than 4 cards per route by default.
Tracing: UI surfaces only support sampled span list with single-span detail view; flamegraph and span-by-service grouping deferred to v2.
Cost breakdown: show coarse-grained token buckets (prompt, completion, embeddings) per route; per-token line-item and per-user attribution hidden behind feature flag.
Performance: console API p95 for dashboard queries < 250ms for common queries (7d window) on staging workloads mirroring production sample.
Storage: telemetry retention capped at 7 days for v1 and configurable via enterprise contract; retention enforcement audited and tested.
Graceful degradation: when cost/trace enrichment fails, console must surface a clear degraded state and still show primary metrics; no page-level errors.
Observability: include metrics for dashboard query latency, trace sampling rate, and enrichment fail-rate; dashboards for these metrics exist in Grafana and are linked in artifacts.
Rollout: feature-toggle gated rollout with canary to 5% of orgs before broader release; rollback plan documented and automated via the release pipeline.
decisions: Cut list: removed per-span flamegraph, per-user cost attribution, and full-traffic trace replay from v1 to meet compute and cost targets.
Sampling: default trace sampling will be set to 0.5% for customers under the free tier and 1% for paying tenants; sampling rate exposed as org-level config behind an enterprise toggle.

Enrichment: disable optional embedding and NER enrichment for dashboard events in v1 to avoid additional embedding calls; enrichment remains a mapped telemetry tag for future enrichment-on-demand flows.
Retention: 7-day retention default for all telemetry in v1 to keep storage and query latency predictable; enterprise customers can request extended retention via Private/Dedicated plans.
Visibility: collapse route-level card sets to a single compact view with a ‘Show more’ link for power users; helps reduce front-end render and data volume.
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial triage — collected stakeholder inputs from Observability, Runtime, and Solutions Engineering. Noted that cost widget was generating disproportionate embedding calls (approx 3x per-route) in staging.

2026-03-05: Design walkthrough — Sophie and design created compact card mocks (Figma link) that reduce card count and use progressive reveal for deeper metrics. Action: Engineering to estimate dashboard query savings.
2026-03-08: Eng estimate: 8 points. Backend changes required: telemetry retention enforcement, query aggregation endpoints, and a sampling adapter for tracing ingestion.
2026-03-10: Security review pre-check — no new PII allowed in v1 telemetry. Confirmed with Security (internal ticket SEC-1142).
2026-03-12: QA gating defined — smoke tests for degraded enrichment, retention enforcement tests, and sampling rate verification. Added acceptance criteria metrics.
2026-03-14: Draft PRD updated with QA checklist and rollback steps; this ticket moved to 'In Review' pending engineering sign-off on query latency SLOs.
